# JSON logs to stdout, one request id generated by us and carried into every worker job

```
ADR id ............ FR-ADR-056
Pack .............. PACK-OPS
Decision type ..... CLIENT_RULING
Decision owner .... client
Decision status ... APPROVED
Decision outcome .. ADOPTED
Decided by ........ Aniruddha Jathar (SRC-003)
Decision date ..... 2026-08-14
Source ............ SRC-002 §5.4.5; SRC-002 §7.6; SRC-002 §7.3; SRC-002 §5.2.6; SRC-001 §8.2; SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01
Constitution ...... frontrow-constitution@0.1.0
```

## Context

`SRC-002 §5.4.5` says log to stdout as JSON and do not write log files to disk. `§7.6` adds a request
id propagated through every log line, **including worker jobs triggered by that request**.

That last clause is the hard part. A request id that stops at the API boundary tells the operator
nothing about why a receipt did not arrive, and the receipt is the artefact that matters most
(`FR-ADR-048`).

`SRC-001 §8.2` sets the stakes: no dedicated operations team, so the system must be observable and
recoverable by one person. The logs are what that person has.

## Decision

**JSON, one object per line, to stdout. Never a file on disk.** A file is state on a stateless
container (`§7.3`) and it dies with the container.

**A fixed field set on every line**, so the logs are queryable rather than merely readable:

`timestamp` (UTC, ISO-8601) · `level` · `logger` · `message` · `request_id` · `service`
(`api` / `worker`) · `instance_id`

And where they apply: `user_id`, `route`, `method`, `status_code`, `duration_ms`, `showtime_id`,
`booking_id`, `error_code`.

**One request-id header: `X-Request-Id`.**

**An inbound value is not trusted.** The ALB is internet-facing, so a client can send any header it
likes, and a forged or duplicated id makes the log correlation worse than having none. **A fresh id is
always generated.** If a client sent one it is recorded as `client_request_id` — a separate field,
never the one used for correlation.

**The generated id is returned in the response `X-Request-Id` header**, and shown to the customer on a
5xx (`FR-ADR-052`), so the one-person operations team can find the request from what the customer
quotes.

**Propagation into the worker is explicit, through the message payload.** The `request_id` of the
request that created the booking is written onto the outbox row (`FR-ADR-031`), travels in the queue
message, and is bound to the worker's logging context for the whole job. `§7.6` requires exactly this
and it is the only way one search finds both halves of a booking.

**The worker also logs its own `job_id`**, because one request can produce several deliveries under
at-least-once (`FR-ADR-032`).

**Log levels:** `INFO` by default in every environment, from `LOG_LEVEL`. `DEBUG` is available and is
not the default anywhere, because CloudWatch holds 5 GB on the free tier (`§5.2.6`).

**What is logged at which level, because this is where volume comes from:**

- One `INFO` line per completed request, with route, status and duration. Not one per log statement
  inside it.
- **`/health/live` and `/health/ready` are not logged at `INFO`.** The ALB polls them continuously and
  they would dominate the volume. Failures are logged.
- A `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` outcome is `INFO` with a counter, not `WARNING`. It is the guard working
  (`FR-ADR-029`), and logging correct behaviour as a warning trains the operator to ignore warnings.
- Unhandled exceptions are `ERROR` with a stack trace. The trace goes in the log and never in the
  response (`FR-ADR-052`).

**Never logged, at any level:**

- **No card data**, ever (`OPEN-PAY-01`, Art V.7). There is none in the system, and the rule stays
  stated so nobody adds a card-shaped log field out of habit.
- No password, no password hash, no JWT, no session cookie, no `Authorization` header.
- No booking reference in a log line that also carries the customer's email. Together they are enough
  to walk into a hall.
- **No resolved secret values.** The boot-time configuration log redacts them (`FR-ADR-053`).
- No full request bodies.

**Redaction is a filter on the logging pipeline, not a discipline at each call site.** A denylist of
field names is applied centrally, so forgetting at one call site does not leak.

## Alternatives rejected

**Trust an inbound `X-Request-Id`.** Rejected above. It is the common pattern behind a trusted proxy
and this ALB is not one.

**Use the ALB's `X-Amzn-Trace-Id` as the correlation id.** Rejected as the primary. It is AWS-specific
and absent locally, so the local and deployed code paths would differ. It is recorded as an additional
field when present, which is genuinely useful for correlating with ALB access logs.

**Propagate the request id through a thread-local or context variable into the worker.** Impossible —
the worker is a different process on a different container. It has to travel in the message.

**Log to a file and ship it with a sidecar.** Rejected by `§5.4.5` and `§7.3`, and a sidecar is another
container inside a 1 GB budget.

**`DEBUG` by default in the deployed environment while learning.** Rejected on the 5 GB allowance, and
because debug logging of request bodies is how card-shaped data would arrive in a log if the system
ever had any.

**Log every health check for completeness.** Rejected on volume.

## Source

`SRC-002 §5.4.5` (JSON to stdout, no files) · `§7.6` (request id through every line including worker
jobs) · `§7.3` (stateless) · `§5.2.6` (5 GB of CloudWatch logs) ·
`SRC-001 §8.2` (observable by one person) · `SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01` (no card data).

The header choice, the trust decision, the field set and the redaction filter are the build session's
under Art III.9.

## Consequences

**Container stdout dies with the container unless a log driver is configured.** `GOTCHAS.md` records
it: with the default driver, the record of a crash loop is destroyed by the restart that caused it.
Configuring the `awslogs` driver is **Zone C**, it needs a prep-queue row, and without it this entire
record delivers nothing. That is the single most important consequence here and it must be said in
chat before Phase 1 deploys, under Art VIII.4.

CloudWatch log retention is a Zone C setting. The default is never-expire, which will consume the 5 GB
allowance eventually. The specification should recommend a finite retention and say what is lost.

The request id joins the audit row (`FR-ADR-019`), the outbox row, the queue message and the customer's
error screen. One search across a log group answers "what happened to this booking" end to end, which
is what `§7.6` is for.

Excluding health checks from `INFO` means the logs do not prove the ALB is polling. That is what the
ALB's own metrics are for.
